title: PersistentVolumes & PersistentVolumeClaims 🧾
description: Decouple storage from Pods using PV and PVC abstractions.

slides.title: The Problem with Hard‑Coded Volumes 🎯
slides.content:
# Pod specs shouldn’t know about storage details

A developer shouldn’t need to know the EBS volume ID or NFS server IP. Kubernetes introduces two API objects:
- **PersistentVolume (PV)** – a piece of storage in the cluster (provisioned by admin or dynamically).
- **PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC)** – a request for storage by a user.

Pods reference PVCs, not specific PVs. This is similar to how a Pod requests CPU/memory without knowing the node.

slides.title: PersistentVolume (PV) 🗄️
slides.content:
## Cluster‑wide storage resource

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: pv-aws
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 20Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  awsElasticBlockStore:
    volumeID: vol-0a1b2c3d
    fsType: ext4
```

- PV is a cluster resource (not namespaced).
- It has a lifecycle independent of any Pod.
- It can be statically created or dynamically provisioned.

slides.title: Access Modes 🔑
slides.content:
## How PVs can be mounted

- **ReadWriteOnce (RWO)** – read/write by a single node (common for block storage).
- **ReadOnlyMany (ROX)** – read‑only by many nodes.
- **ReadWriteMany (RWX)** – read/write by many nodes (requires shared filesystem like NFS, CephFS).

Not all storage backends support all modes.

quizData.question: Which access mode allows a volume to be written from multiple nodes simultaneously?
quizData.explanation: RWX volumes support concurrent read‑write from multiple nodes.

slides.title: PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) 📋
slides.content:
## A user’s request for storage

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: my-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 10Gi
```

- PVC is namespaced.
- Kubernetes finds a matching PV (size >= request, matching access modes).
- If no PV matches, the PVC stays Pending until one is available (or dynamic provisioning kicks in).

slides.title: Create PVC
slides.codeSnippet:
kubectl apply -f pvc.yaml
kubectl get pvc

slides.title: Using PVC in a Pod 🔌
slides.content:
## Finally, mount it!

```yaml
spec:
  volumes:
  - name: app-storage
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: my-pvc
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx
    volumeMounts:
    - name: app-storage
      mountPath: /var/data
```

The Pod doesn’t know anything about the underlying storage – just the PVC name.

quizData.question: What happens if a PVC requests 5Gi and no PV has that capacity?

options.text: The Pod using it starts anyway
The PVC stays Pending until a matching PV appears or dynamic provisioning creates one

quizData.explanation: PVC waits for a suitable PV; with dynamic provisioning, a StorageClass can auto‑create it.

slides.title: Reclaim Policy ♻️
slides.content:
## What happens when PVC is deleted?

- **Retain** – PV is released but not deleted; admin must manually clean up the data.
- **Delete** – both PV and the associated storage asset (e.g., cloud disk) are deleted.
- **Recycle** – deprecated; basic scrub (`rm -rf /`) and make available again.

Set in the PV’s `persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy`.

quizData.question: True or False: The 'Delete' reclaim policy automatically removes the cloud disk when the PVC is deleted.
quizData.explanation: With 'Delete', the underlying storage asset is deleted along with the PV.
